title: Degree cap for sections with prescribed vanishing on a smooth proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], let $C$ be a smooth proper connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $A$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Put $e=\deg_k A$, with degree defined by $\deg_k M=\chi(C,M)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle, def-pc-euler-characteristic]. For an effective divisor $B=\sum_P n_P[P]$ of degree $b=\sum_P n_P$ [def-sc-divisor], and integers $m,q\ge0$, the space of sections of $A^{\otimes m}$ vanishing to order at least $q n_P$ at each $P$ is $H^0(C,A^{\otimes m}(-qB))$ [def-sc-rational-section-divisor, def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. It is finite-dimensional and satisfies
$$\deg_k(A^{\otimes m}(-qB))=me-qb,\qquad h^0(C,A^{\otimes m}(-qB))\le\max\{me-qb+1,0\}.$$
The maximum is taken in $\mathbf Z$ and $h^0$ denotes dimension over $k$. In particular it is zero if $me-qb<0$. The zero divisor and $m=0$ or $q=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0CCS, lemma-grd-inequalities, r <= d; with varieties.tex Tags 0AYX (lemma-degree-tensor-product) and 0AYY (lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor). Negative degree case by the effective zero divisor of a nonzero section. Agent formulation for tensor powers and imposed divisors.

proof.text: Put $L=A^{\otimes m}\otimes\mathcal O_C(-qB)$. The divisor-module local description gives $\mathcal O_C(-qB)_P=t^{qn_P}\mathcal O_{C,P}$ for a uniformizer $t$, and gives $\mathcal O_C(0)=\mathcal O_C$. Tensor products of invertible modules are invertible, so induction on $m$ (starting with $\mathcal O_C$) shows that $L$ is invertible. In a local basis of $A^{\otimes m}$, a germ belongs to $L_P$ exactly when its coefficient lies in $t^{qn_P}\mathcal O_{C,P}$, that is, has valuation at least $qn_P$. Thus the subsheaf $L\subseteq A^{\otimes m}$ consists exactly of sections with the specified vanishing, including the zero section; away from the finite support the condition is just regularity. Taking global sections gives the space stated in the item, with $H^0=\Gamma$ for module cohomology.

source.place: Tags 0BE9 (local divisor modules), 01CT (tensor products of invertible modules); cohomology.tex Tag 01DZ for degree zero

proof.text: The degree definition gives $\deg\mathcal O_C=\chi(\mathcal O_C)-\chi(\mathcal O_C)=0$. By tensor-degree additivity, induction gives $\deg A^{\otimes0}=0$ and $\deg A^{\otimes(m+1)}=me+e$, hence $\deg A^{\otimes m}=me$. The effective divisor $qB$ has degree $qb$, so degree agreement gives $\deg\mathcal O_C(qB)=qb$. Divisor-module multiplication identifies $\mathcal O_C(-qB)\otimes\mathcal O_C(qB)$ with $\mathcal O_C(0)=\mathcal O_C$. Additivity therefore gives $\deg\mathcal O_C(-qB)=-qb$ and $d:=\deg L=me-qb$. These calculations also cover $m=0$, $q=0$, and $B=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AYX, lemma-degree-tensor-product; Tag 0AYY, lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor; degree agreement for effective divisors

proof.text: Since $C$ is proper over the field $k$ and $L$ is invertible, the proper-field coherence lemma makes $L$ coherent and $C$ Noetherian. Apply proper coherent cohomology to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: the base is the spectrum of the Noetherian ring $k$, so $H^0(C,L)$ is a finite $k$-module, hence a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space. Thus $h^0(C,L)$ is an ordinary nonnegative integer.

source.place: Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian; Tags 02O5/02O6, proper coherent cohomology

proof.text: Assume $s\in H^0(C,L)$ is nonzero. The smooth-connected-curve local-ring theorem makes $C$ integral. Hence the nonzero-section Cartier lemma applies: the zero scheme $D=Z(s)$ is an effective Cartier divisor, and in every nonempty trivializing affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ the coordinate $a$ of $s$ is a nonzerodivisor and $D\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/(a))$. The zero-scheme divisor isomorphism gives $L\cong\mathcal O_C(D)$. Since $C$ is proper of dimension one, the Cartier-divisor finiteness lemma gives $D$ finite over $k$. This includes the empty zero scheme of a nowhere-vanishing section.

source.place: Tag 0CCS, lemma-grd-inequalities, first paragraph; divisors.tex Tags 02OR/01X0 and varieties.tex Tag 0AYY

proof.text: The restriction $L|_D$ is invertible: restrict any local basis of $L$ to $D$. Apply finite-morphism trivialization to $D\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and its unique base point. Its nonempty open neighborhood is all of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $L|_D\cong\mathcal O_D$. Consequently $\Gamma(D,L|_D)\cong\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)$ as $k$-vector spaces. The effective-Cartier clause of degree-base-change, applied on the proper one-dimensional scheme $C$, says that the latter space is finite-dimensional and has dimension $\deg\mathcal O_C(D)$. By the isomorphism in Step 4, this is $d$. In particular, the existence of $s\ne0$ forces $d\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 0CCS, lemma-grd-inequalities, finite-zero-scheme calculation; divisors.tex Tag 0BUT and varieties.tex Tag 0AYY

proof.text: Locally in the notation of Step 4, multiplication by $s$ and restriction give $0\to R\xrightarrow{\,a\,}Re\to(R/(a))e\to0$: the first map is injective because $a$ is a nonzerodivisor, and the quotient is exactly the last term. Thus globally $0\to\mathcal O_C\xrightarrow{s}L\to i_*(L|_D)\to0$, where $i:D\hookrightarrow C$. Global sections are left exact, and by definition $\Gamma(C,i_*(L|_D))=\Gamma(D,L|_D)$. Global functions on the proper smooth connected curve are $k$. We get an exact sequence $0\to k\to H^0(C,L)\to\Gamma(D,L|_D)$ with no surjectivity assertion at the right. The kernel has dimension one and the image has dimension at most $d$ by Step 5: lift a basis of the image and adjoin a basis of the kernel to obtain a basis of $H^0(C,L)$. Hence $h^0(C,L)\le1+d$ whenever there is a nonzero section.

source.place: Tag 0CCS, lemma-grd-inequalities, short exact sequence and dimension inequality; divisors.tex Tag 0C6K, remark-ses-regular-section

proof.text: If there is no nonzero section, then $H^0(C,L)=0$ and $h^0(C,L)=0\le\max\{d+1,0\}$. Otherwise Step 5 gives $d\ge0$, so $\max\{d+1,0\}=d+1$ and Step 6 proves the required inequality. In particular $d<0$ excludes any nonzero section. Substituting $d=me-qb$ from Step 2 proves every assertion, with the maximum interpreted in $\mathbf Z$.

lean.statement: theorem smoothCurve_section_degree_cap (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (C : Scheme.{u}) [C.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsConnectedCurve (C ↘ Spec (.of k))] [Smooth (C ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsProper (C ↘ Spec (.of k))] (A : C.Modules) [A.IsInvertible] (B : C.Divisor) (hB : ∀ P : closedPoints C, 0 ≤ B P) (m q : ℕ) : (∃ j : smoothCurveVanishingSections k C A B m q →ₗ[k] ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor C.toRingedSpace ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars (globalSectionsRingHom k (X := C))).obj (A.tensorPow m)), Function.Injective j ∧ ∀ s : Γ(A.tensorPow m, ⊤), s ∈ Set.range j ↔ smoothCurveSectionVanishes k C (C ↘ Spec (.of k)) (A.tensorPow m) B q s) ∧ FiniteDimensional k (smoothCurveVanishingSections k C A B m q) ∧ (smoothCurveVanishingTwist k C (C ↘ Spec (.of k)) A B m q).degree k = (m : ℤ) * A.degree k - (q : ℤ) * Divisor.degree C B ∧ (Module.finrank k (smoothCurveVanishingSections k C A B m q) : ℤ) ≤ max ((m : ℤ) * A.degree k - (q : ℤ) * Divisor.degree C B + 1) 0 ∧ ((m : ℤ) * A.degree k - (q : ℤ) * Divisor.degree C B < 0 → Subsingleton (smoothCurveVanishingSections k C A B m q))
